title: Resolved coefficient Hom tower comparison map is invertible levelwise

lean.statement:
theorem integralDualizing_coefficient_hom_tower_comparison :
    ∃ α : integralDualizingCoefficientHomTower l E ⋙
        CoefTower.totalLimit (integralDualizingCoefficients l E) ⟶
      coefficientDerivedDual (integralDualizingCoefficients l E),
      ∀ C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
        (integralDualizingCoefficients l E)),
        IsIso (α.app (op C))

proof.text: For any strong monoidal adjunction F ⊣ G between closed monoidal categories, take mates of the tensor comparison to construct G([F(C),Y]) ≅ [C,G(Y)], naturally in C. Apply this to the derived constant-tower functor. Its strong monoidal structure is the exact-derived tensor structure; constant towers preserve flat objects because finite limits and tensor products are computed at each level. Transport the constant/limit adjunction through the unique equivalence between the small and standard tower localizations.

Compute the derived inverse limit of the quotient tower concentrated in degree zero. The normalized strict Roos comparison identifies the right-derived limit with the shifted cone of one minus shift on the degreewise product. Surjective quotient transitions make this map degreewise epic by recursive lifting; its kernel is the ordinary limit. The degreewise-epic kernel-to-shifted-cone quasi-isomorphism thus identifies the derived limit with that ordinary limit.

Construct the ordinary quotient-tower cone from the actual scalar reductions. Profinite completeness says every compatible family has a unique preimage in the integral coefficient ring, so this cone is limiting (restriction of scalars retains the underlying maps). Commuting the degree-zero single-complex functor with limits identifies the derived quotient limit with the tensor unit. Substitute this unit isomorphism in the natural closed-adjunction comparison and take its hom, obtaining isomorphic components at every coefficient complex.
